body.statement: If \(t>d/2\), then over every law in \(\mathcal M\) and every design density satisfying \(c_X\le f_X\le C_X\), a finite-order cross-fitted empirical higher-order SCoDiTE test has uniform type-I error at most \(\alpha+o(1)\) and uniform type-II error at most \(\beta+o(1)\) whenever \(\|\Psi(P)\|_{\mathcal H}\ge Cn^{-1/2}\). Thus \(\delta_n^\star\le Cn^{-1/2}\); this upper bound uses only the declared model assumptions, its correction has \(M=o(n)\), and it imposes no smoothness on \(f_X\). For the reverse inequality only, impose the class-richness premise that \(\mathcal M\) contains a path \((P_\theta)_{|\theta|\le\varepsilon_0}\) supported on \(\{y_-,y_+\}\), with \(P_0\in\mathcal M_0\), fixed \(P_X\) and \(e\), constant contrast \(U_{P_\theta}(x)=\theta b_Y\), nonzero derivative \(w_0=E_{P_0}[K_X]\otimes b_Y\), quadratic-mean differentiability at zero with Fisher information strictly between zero and infinity, and \(\sup_{|\theta|\le\varepsilon_0}\sum_{j\ge1}\mu_j(P_\theta)^{-2s}|\langle w_0,v_j(P_\theta)\rangle_{\mathcal H}|^2<\infty\). Under this premise, the local two-point reduction gives \(\delta_n^\star\ge cn^{-1/2}\), and hence \(\delta_n^\star\asymp n^{-1/2}\).
body.justification: The high-smoothness upper bound isolates density-robust higher-order correction, while the explicitly conditional local-path reduction supplies only the ordinary parametric lower bound and is not the nuisance-rate crux.
body.gap: Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins prove semiparametric efficiency for the scalar mean under missing at random and a broader scalar doubly robust class using an empirical Gram basis of dimension \(k=o(n)\); they do not prove a Hilbert-valued testing expansion or uniform exact-null calibration.
body.consumer: It supplies a primitive size guarantee for SCoDiTE applications with nonuniform covariates whenever total nuisance smoothness is above the elbow, and states exactly when that upper rate is also a minimax equality.
